newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Interest seen in Telebras calls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Interest seen in Telebras calls.

text.p: Interest remained heavy in call options on American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of Brazil's Telebras, traders said Monday.
At the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) last Friday an investor did a large spread in Telebras options, buying the February 90 calls and selling the February 85 puts.
That same investor continued the strategy on Monday, but other investors were attracted to the February and March calls also, traders said.
In late trading, Telebras shares in the U.S. were up 7/8 at 88-1/8 on consolidated volume of 1.6 million shares.

The stock hit a new 52-week peak of 88-5/8 intraday. ADR traders said the stock was boosted by speculation on the Sao Paulo exchange and the possibility that Brazil could sign private cellular concession contracts earlier than planned.

On the American Stock Exchange, the Telebras February 90 call traded 5,820 contracts, the March 90 call traded 2,800 and the April 90 call traded about 640. The February 80 put traded 1,300 and the February 85 put traded 6,300.
"It's one customer buying calls and selling puts," a trader in Chicago said of the February 90 call-February 85 put activity. "It's a continuation" from Friday.
Telbras options trade at the AMEX and on the Chicago Board Options Exchange, Philadelphia Stock Exchange and New York Stock Exchange.
"What's more interesting is that there's substantial customer demand for calls in February and March," an options trader at the AMEX said.
"There is a very slight uptick in volatility but there is enormous demand for calls," he said.
He added that the interest appeared to be coming from a "professional" overseas investor.
In other options activity, LEAPS, or long term equity anticipation securities, continued to draw interest.
On the AMEX, the Intel Corp January 1998 180 call traded about 1,875 contracts. The option, which had open interest of 2,384, was up 1-5/8 at 19-3/8.
The Intel January 1998 205 call traded a heavy 4,415 contracts. Its open interest was 777. The option rose 7/8 to 11-3/8.
Underlying Intel shares rose 1-5/8 to 163-7/8, backing off a new intraday 52-week high reached at 165. More than 9.6 million Intel shares changed hands.
Several regular-length Intel options were actively traded, particularly around the 160, 165 and 170 strike prices.
Among other LEAPS, the Federal Express Corp January 1998 32-1/2 call traded 2,890 contracts.
The option, which had open interest of 16,744 contracts, was up 1/8 at 20-7/8.
Regular-length options on Federal Express were thinly traded.
Federal Express shares eased 1/4 to 51 on consolidated volume of about 550,000 shares. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
